BiblicalUsage: leqeṭ means the gleaning — a small word with a sharp edge. In Leviticus 19:9, "neither shalt thou gather the gleanings of thy harvest."; and in Leviticus 23:22, "neither shalt thou gather any gleaning of thy harvest: thou shalt leave them unto the poor".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the gleanings belong to the poor by law — God told Israel not to reap the corners, so the stranger and the fatherless could eat.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
